title: State, refactoring and the feature arc
dek: Terraform's record of what exists is one plaintext JSON document per workspace, and its consistency rests on advisory locks rather than compare-and-swap. This third part of a four-part teardown reads Terraform v1.17.0's state managers, the lock each backend builds from its own storage (and the S3 configuration that builds none), workspaces and remote state as non-boundaries, the refactoring blocks that moved state surgery into the plan, and the 1.5 to 1.17 feature arc: import, check, tests with mocks, provider functions, ephemeral values and write-only arguments, list resources, actions, and the surfaces that are still gated or run out of process.
byline: 24 October 2026 · Subject: terraform@018a99c8 (v1.17.0) · Part 3 of 4 · Read from the source; measured on this machine with no cloud credentials
description: Terraform v1.17.0 taken apart, part 3: the v4 state file, lineage and serial, locks per backend and the S3 default with no lock, workspaces and terraform_remote_state, moved/removed/import blocks, and the 1.5 to 1.17 features from check and terraform test to ephemeral values, query, actions, deferral, Stacks and Policy.
og_description: Part 3 of a four-part Terraform teardown at v1.17.0 (018a99c8): state is one plaintext JSON document guarded by advisory locks; S3 with neither use_lockfile nor DynamoDB takes no lock; -lock-timeout defaults to one attempt; terraform_remote_state strips sensitivity; refactoring blocks run inside plan; almost every feature since 1.5 is a schema, a node and an RPC; -invoke silently turns a plan refresh-only; Policy fails open for plan and apply.

from the code marks a fact read from hashicorp/terraform at v1.17.0 (018a99c83c5d, 21 October 2026), cited as a path and line range from the repository root. Where a behaviour has changed since the tag, the upstream status is given against origin/main at a060ad5a1b (23 October 2026). measured here marks output from the v1.17.0 binary on a 2-vCPU Linux box with the providers random 3.9.1 and aws 6.70.0 from a shared plugin cache. No cloud credentials existed. Nothing was applied to a cloud: the state experiments used local state, a toy HTTP server and the built-in terraform_data; the AWS examples used fake credentials (AKIAFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKE with the skip switches) or mock_provider. One action example sent a request to AWS with the fake key, which was rejected; §09 lists every such request. Timings depend on page cache and load and are given as ranges. reconstruction marks a judgement drawn from those sources rather than read in one place. Findings carry their status; none was reported upstream.

This is Part 3 of 4 of Terraform, taken apart. Part 1 covers the HCL language, values and how init turns a directory into a configuration tree. Part 2 builds and walks the plan graph, follows providers as child processes over gRPC and shows that apply re-plans. Part 4 builds one project on AWS, GCP and Azure with no credentials, covers the licence and the fork, and ends with the findings register.
